title: Markov Blanket Artifact v0.1
description: A grow-shrink Markov blanket, with the sufficient statistic it was computed from and the definition check it passed. A standalone artifact: it says its own `kind`, which is how `themis.audits.artifact_of` recognises it and how `verify_markov_blanket` refuses a foreign dict. What makes it worth declaring rather than merely producing is the audit trail — the recorded correlation matrix or joint counts are what let a second implementation redo every conditional-independence test WITHOUT the data, and a field silently dropped from that record turns an auditable claim into an unauditable one with no visible difference.

target.description: The variable whose blanket this is.

blanket.description: The blanket itself, sorted. A local screen — parents, children, spouses — and NOT an adjustment set: conditioning on a child or a spouse when estimating an effect is a collider open, which is why the note beside it says so in words too.

columns.description: The search space this blanket came out of: the target first, then the candidate pool in the order it was given. `blanket` is a subset of the tail of this. Distinct from `data_columns` (#384): this is what the SEARCH ranged over, that is what the DIGEST covers, and they are the same set here only because the search is what was hashed.

data_columns.description: The columns `data_hash` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator that makes the digest a claim about something (#381). Without it two differing digests can only say "not the same run", never whether what changed was the measurements or which columns were measured.

method.description: The search. One value today; declared as an enum rather than a free string because the audit re-runs the search, and an audit that does not know which search it is re-running is not one.

test.description: The conditional-independence test, chosen by the data type of the columns: all-continuous → Fisher-Z, all-discrete → chi-square, a mix → the homogeneous conditional-Gaussian likelihood ratio (Lauritzen & Wermuth 1989). This value also decides WHICH sufficient statistic is recorded below — the two are one decision, and the branch says so. The third was chosen out of the mixed tests that exist ON that property: a kernel test's sufficient statistic is the n×n Gram matrix and a rank test's is the ranks, which is to say the data, and an artifact that has to carry the data in order to be audited is not one. What this test costs instead is a premise — one covariance shared across the discrete configurations — and a premise is a thing this package can carry. Its two degenerate points are the other two tests: with no discrete column G² is −n·log(1−ρ²), the likelihood ratio the Fisher-Z transform approximates, and with no continuous column it is the deviance form of the same test Pearson's statistic estimates, on the same degrees of freedom.

alpha.description: The level every test below was read at. Part of the artifact because the blanket is only a blanket AT a level: the same p-values at a different alpha are a different blanket.

tests.description: The definition check, one entry per candidate. Completeness: every non-member is independent of the target given the whole blanket (`role: shield`). Minimality: every member is dependent given the REST of the blanket (`role: necessary`). Together they are the definition of a Markov blanket, which is why this is the artifact and the blanket alone is not. The three entry shapes share a head but are declared separately rather than composed, so each can close itself with `additionalProperties: false` — they are told apart by WHICH statistic they carry, and a branch that admitted unknown keys could not tell them apart at all. That rule is why the conditional-Gaussian entry names its statistic `likelihood_ratio` rather than reusing `statistic`: it IS a likelihood ratio and not a Pearson statistic, and a third shape spelled like the second would leave the `oneOf` above unable to say which it had — the naming and the discrimination are one decision.

note.description: What the run says about itself, one statement per sentence: the blanket it found with the search and test by their published names, and that this is a screening set and NOT an adjustment set. The second is why the field is not merely a summary — the blanket holds children and spouses, and conditioning on those is the one mistake a reader can make with it. Statements and not text: this was a `string` until #469, so the producer wrote the sentence and therefore chose the language, and the two enums above are excused from a gloss ON THE GROUNDS that this field names them to a person.

correlation.description: Fisher-Z path only: the correlation matrix over `columns`, in that order — the sufficient statistic for every partial correlation below. Present exactly when `test` is `fisherz`.

contingency.description: Chi-square path only: the joint counts over `columns` — the sufficient statistic for every chi-square below. Present exactly when `test` is `chisq`.

conditional_gaussian.description: Conditional-Gaussian path only: which columns are discrete and which continuous, the integer coding of the discrete ones, and one row per OCCUPIED configuration. Present exactly when `test` is `cg_lrt`.

passed.description: Whether this test agrees with the role: a `necessary` member must be dependent (p <= alpha), a `shield` non-member independent (p > alpha). Recorded rather than left to the reader because the comparison direction differs by role.

likelihood_ratio.description: G² = 2[l(XYS) + l(S) − l(XS) − l(YS)], over the four homogeneous conditional-Gaussian fits the test compares. Named for what it is rather than reusing `statistic`, which is what tells this entry shape apart from the chi-square one beside it.

dof.description: The same signed combination over the four fits, each counted as (∏k − 1) multinomial parameters + |C|·∏k means + |C|(|C|+1)/2 covariance entries. Recorded rather than left to the reader because it is not a function of the two variables' cardinalities alone — which is precisely how it differs from the chi-square entry, where it is.

conditionalGaussian.description: The sufficient statistic for every conditional-Gaussian test in this artifact. Every set of columns a test asks about is a MARGINAL of this one — dropping a discrete column adds cells together, dropping a continuous one drops a row and a column of the two arrays below — which is what lets one record serve four fits per test without the data.

discrete.description: The discrete columns, in the order a configuration below is indexed by. A subset of `columns` and not a reordering of it: the statistic's own order is what the cells are keyed by, and the search's order is what `blanket` is read against.

continuous.description: The continuous columns, in the order the sum vector and the cross-product matrix below are indexed by. At least one, because with none of them this would be the chi-square path.

levels.description: Per DISCRETE column, in `discrete` order, the distinct values in the integer coding — index i of a configuration means this list's element i.

cells.description: One row per occupied discrete configuration: [configuration, count, sum of the continuous vector, sum of its outer products]. Sparse for the reason the contingency table is — the product of the cardinalities is mostly empty — so the size is bounded by the number of distinct discrete rows rather than by that product. The last two entries are what the pooled covariance is assembled from: Σᵢ(crossᵢ − nᵢ·μᵢμᵢ'), the one covariance the homogeneity premise says every configuration shares.

prefixItems.description: One level index per column of `discrete`.

levels.description: Per column of `columns`, in that order, the distinct values in the integer coding — index i of a configuration below means this list's element i.

counts.description: The non-zero cells of the joint table, as [configuration, count] pairs. Sparse on purpose: a full table is the product of the cardinalities and is mostly zeros.

prefixItems.description: One level index per column of `columns`.
